title: Package-draft batch publish (Studio "publish whole app") still answers success with no sign when an object's storage sync is refused
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cyvF7SP65frVFAYLv7

Filing gate: ① a public door's wrong answer with a named producer: `publishPackageDrafts` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (the `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts` door, Studio's "publish whole app"). Found by the #30635 dev (PR #30691, out of its surface, stopped there by order), read by the seat on the PR head `9c02a3e7`. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested grade: p3 (the same family as #30635, on the third door).
Dedupe: `publishPackageDrafts storage`, `storageRefused`, `object-storage-sync-refused` — no open card; nearest #30635 (the save and single-item publish doors, PR #30691). **New.**
Reader: `domain:server` (`metadata-protocol`). Serial: after PR #30691 lands; `protocol.ts` is a hot file (#29985 codemod, #30020), so the seat checks the serial queue before dispatch.

## What happens

After PR #30691, a save in publish mode and `POST /meta/:type/:name/publish` answer a refused object storage sync with one `warning` advisory (rule `object-storage-sync-refused`) on their existing `advisories`. The batch door runs the same sync through `runPublishSideEffects` (`protocol.ts`, the per-item loop of `publishPackageDrafts`, ~L12469 on `9c02a3e7`) and gets the same `storageRefused` back, but drops it: the `published[]` element for that object is pushed BEFORE the side effects run, and nothing reads `eff.storageRefused`. So "publish whole app" still answers success with no sign that an object's table was not created or altered; only the server log says so (#22985).

## Expected

- The batch answer tells the caller, on the existing per-element `published[].advisories` (already declared on the batch response; omitted when empty), the same `object-storage-sync-refused` warning the single-item doors give. No new key, status unchanged, the publish not failed.
- Pins through the door: a refused sync on one object of a batch → that element carries the advisory, the others do not; a clean batch → no `advisories` added.
- If the element cannot carry it without a spec change, stop and report: that is a spec-lane change.
